atoms.reason: Foundational meta-structure: a single canonical JSON with required fields, one concrete file:path per atom, no multi-file changes, and explicit_no_new_layer=true. Machine-checkable test (ConvertFrom-Json + field/uniqueness assertions). This is the spine the rest of the wave hangs on; cheap, reversible, high-leverage.

Consensus (A,B). Correctly quarantines A12/A13 as underspecified new-verification-layer risk and defers error-contract enforcement to a separate direction. Strong scope-creep control with an explicit rejected_atoms assertion; directly serves the no-new-layer principle.

Test-only atom pinning router behavior: plan-refinement DISCUSS without [[HIGH-STAKES]] -> Standard, explicit marker -> High-Stakes, broad arch -> Deep. Concrete named test file, zero behavior change. Lower impact (coverage), but locks the contract for ATOM_004.

Implementation pair to ATOM_003: narrows elevation in lib/decision-depth.ps1 so 'discuss/refine/atom-list' alone does not force Deep/High-Stakes. Consistent with ATOM_010's router-precision lever. Medium reversibility and a softly-specified 'paired S1T' test hold the score down; behavior change in a routing path warrants the test from ATOM_003 landing first.

Chosen resolution of the A15 conflict: reuse the existing duplicate_of/resolved_reason representation (1 representative open, 4 rejected), no new count/first_seen/last_seen fields. Best aligned with explicit_no_new_layer (ATOM_021) and minimal-change philosophy; concrete test. Judge resolves the A15 data-model collision in favor of this no-new-field approach.

Implementation pair to ATOM_005: strengthen the existing Invoke-BacklogDuplicateCompactor path to reject typed audit duplicates via duplicate_of/duplicate_key/resolved_reason, no append-site collapse. Reuses existing code; medium reversibility. Must be implemented to match ATOM_005's no-new-field record (not ATOM_012/015).

Test-only stale-start coverage in test-audit-launch-guard.ps1: dead stale start -> abandoned + next admission allowed; live pid blocks; recent dead pid within TTL still blocks. Cheap, reversible, encodes the exact contract ATOM_008 implements.

Implementation pair to ATOM_007: terminalize stale dead-pid starts as decision='abandoned' via existing reconciliation/ledger writers and exclude abandoned run_id from attempt count. Signal-hygiene win reusing existing infra; medium reversibility, 'paired A10T' test.

Consensus (A,B). Makes Get-StaleAuditLaunchInfo terminal-aware and routes completion-contract results through the EXISTING auditor stale-alert, classifying benign terminal reasons as non-alerting. Strong false-alert reduction with a crisp criterion (incomplete window -> exactly one alert, benign -> none). Touches multiple behaviors, so simplicity/feasibility are tempered.

penalties.reason: Bundles claim-correction (plan doc) with metrics.jsonl analysis/report — violates the 1-file/1-test atomicity rule from ATOM_011; split into a claim-correction atom and a metrics-analysis atom.

atoms.reason: Consensus (B,C) and the most important correction: deletes the false 'depth-router speeds up Standard plan-only tasks' claim and re-derives real levers from data (verify_ms = gate-regression scope narrowing; planner_ms = router precision on SYNTHESIS-routed DISCUSS). Correct and high-impact, but it bundles analysis + doc edits with a soft test, so modify and decompose.

Consensus (B,C). Defines the atomicity invariant (1 atom = 1 impl file + 1 dedicated test) and decomposes A10/A11 accordingly. This is the rule that makes the whole list verifiable and safely sequenceable; cheap and reversible.

penalties.reason: Blocking conflict: the 'add duplicate_count + last_seen' clause contradicts the chosen ATOM_005 (no count/first_seen/last_seen fields) and is internally inconsistent with its own 'drop the count/first_seen/last_seen collapse' directive.

atoms.reason: Consensus intent (B,C) to resolve the A15 collision is sound, and dropping the parallel collapse representation is correct. But the embedded 'add duplicate_count+last_seen' instruction collides head-on with ATOM_005 and offers three divergent paths. Modify: keep the collision resolution and the 'safe fallback: drop A15 entirely' branch, strip the field-adding clause so it conforms to ATOM_005.

Adds a pure Get-PhaseLatencyBaseline in existing lib/metrics.ps1 (median/p90 per phase) with a dedicated synthetic-input test. A pure function in an existing lib is not a new layer; it supplies the verify_ms/planner_ms baseline ATOM_010/ATOM_017 depend on. Low risk, well-specified.

Additive 'window_incomplete' ledger decision value with a reason in driver/10-maintenance.ps1, with a focused test (started-without-terminal => exactly one such entry). Reuses Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry; coordinate with ATOM_008/009/016 so the stale-launch family stays coherent.

penalties.reason: Directly conflicts with the chosen ATOM_005 (no count/first_seen/last_seen) and reinforces the contested clause in ATOM_012; introduces a new data-model field the plan otherwise disavows.

atoms.reason: Well-specified in isolation, but it loses the A15 data-representation conflict: adding duplicate_count/last_seen contradicts ATOM_005 and the explicit no-new-field/no-new-layer stance. Reject in favor of ATOM_005's reuse of duplicate_of/resolved_reason; revive only if the project later decides it explicitly wants counts.

Teaches the existing stale-start reconcile (driver/60-startup.ps1 / 10-maintenance.ps1) to treat the 'window_incomplete' value from ATOM_014 as terminal-but-incomplete, preventing false 'still-running'. Sound dependency on ATOM_014; reconcile-case test, with 'expected state' the only soft spot.

penalties.reason: Low reversibility + high cost; narrowing verify scope risks missed regressions if the related-suite mapping is wrong — must land last in the safest-first ordering and behind the ATOM_013 baseline.

atoms.reason: The genuine verify_ms lever from ATOM_010: scope Get-GateRegressionScope to suites related to a single-file core change instead of the ~312.6s ceiling. Highest speed payoff, but riskiest (low reversibility). The test is well-designed to bound the risk — the narrowed scope must still include the suite catching a known-regression fixture and show zero missed regressions — so accept, sequenced last.

Produces the human-facing plan doc (chosen+narrowed directions, quantified justification, ordered atom list, reuse map, explicit no-new-layer statement) with a no-code constraint. The synthesis deliverable of the wave; test ('contains all sections, no implementation code') is adequate though section-presence is shallow.

penalties.reason: Redundant with ATOM_001, which already mandates one concrete file:path per retained atom; keeping both duplicates the requirement.

atoms.reason: Correct requirement (every atom needs a concrete file:path to satisfy success_test #8) but it is subsumed by ATOM_001. Modify: fold this assertion into ATOM_001's schema validation rather than carrying it as a separate atom.

Order the list safest -> most impactful so self-implementation starts with the least risky atom (and lands ATOM_017 last). Strong risk control for a self-modifying bridge; cheap. Test ('ordered by safety') is somewhat soft but workable given each atom's risk/reversibility fields.

The governing constraint: reuse existing logger/config/test-harness, introduce zero new layers or frameworks. It is the principle that disambiguates the A15 conflict toward ATOM_005 and rejects scope creep (ATOM_002). Only weakness is the subjective 'code review confirms' test; pair with the structural checks in ATOM_001 to make it enforceable.
